title: Why Some Seeds Wait
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
When a packet of seeds fails to produce seedlings, we may assume that the seeds have died. In nature, however, delayed germination can be a valuable strategy. If every seed begins growing after the first rainfall, a short wet period followed by drought could destroy an entire generation. A mixture of immediate growth and continued dormancy spreads that risk over time.

An ecologist studying plants on disturbed ground collected seeds from the same species at several sites. In the laboratory, the seeds received equal amounts of water and light. Some germinated within days, while others remained unchanged. To determine whether the waiting seeds were still alive, the team tested a small sample and found healthy tissue inside many of them.

The researchers then exposed separate groups to different sequences of conditions. A single warm, wet week produced little additional growth. Repeated cycles of cooler and warmer temperatures brought many more seeds out of dormancy. The sequence appeared to provide information that one favourable day could not: conditions had been changing over a sustained period rather than briefly improving.

There were also differences between collection sites. Seeds from ground that was regularly disturbed tended to respond more quickly, but the team could not immediately tell whether this reflected inherited traits or conditions experienced by the parent plants. Both explanations remained possible because the plants had not been raised under identical conditions before producing seeds.

For habitat restoration, the findings suggest that low initial germination should not automatically be treated as failure. A seed mixture may contain a reserve that emerges later. Managers still need to check whether the seeds are viable, but discarding every slow batch could remove a useful form of biological insurance.

questions.prompt: What advantage can delayed germination offer a plant population?
options: It protects every seedling from insects.
It guarantees that rainfall will continue.
It spreads the risk of unsuitable conditions over time.
It allows seeds to grow without water.
questions.answer: It spreads the risk of unsuitable conditions over time.
questions.explanation: 延迟萌发可避免所有种子在短暂降雨后一起遭遇干旱，把风险分散到不同时段。

questions.prompt: Why did the researchers examine tissue inside some waiting seeds?
options: To determine whether the seeds were still alive.
To measure the amount of light in the laboratory.
To identify the insects that had visited the parent plants.
To compare the roots of mature plants.
questions.answer: To determine whether the seeds were still alive.
questions.explanation: 检查组织是为了判断未萌发的种子仍有生命力还是已经死亡。

questions.prompt: Which treatment brought more seeds out of dormancy?
options: A longer period with no light.
An increase in the size of the seed containers.
Repeated changes between cooler and warmer temperatures.
questions.answer: Repeated changes between cooler and warmer temperatures.
questions.explanation: 反复的冷暖温度周期使更多种子解除休眠，单次温暖湿润期效果不大。

questions.prompt: What uncertainty remained about differences between collection sites?
options: Whether any seeds had received water.
Whether inheritance or parental growing conditions caused them.
Whether all the sites contained the same soil colour.
Whether the laboratory could measure temperature.
questions.answer: Whether inheritance or parental growing conditions caused them.
questions.explanation: 不同地点的差异可能来自遗传，也可能来自母株经历的环境，实验尚未区分。
